sections.content: How many people are "youth and community workers"?

49,025 people

were counted on the census as "youth and community workers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Youth and community workers provide support to individuals or groups of individuals through a range of activities or services that aim to encourage participation in social and community life and promote personal and social development.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "youth and community workers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "youth and community workers", 12.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "youth and community workers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "youth and community workers" included:

  • protective service associate professionals (other)
  • office supervisors
  • senior care workers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "youth and community workers" there were more women than men (78.8% compared with 21.2%).

This means "youth and community workers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health and social care associate professionals".

Men made up 21.2% and women made up 78.8% of "youth and community workers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "youth and community workers" included:

  • visual merchandisers and related occupations
  • nursing auxiliaries and assistants
  • sales administrators

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "youth and community workers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "youth and community workers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "youth and community workers", 15.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (62.9% compared with 37.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.2%) than self-employed (2.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
